items.title: [Bug] deepseek v3.2/v4 DSML parsing: asserts instead of documented ValueError (silently skipped under -O), batch vs streaming grammar and duplicate-parameter divergences
items.body:
- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.

### Describe the bug

three consistency issues around the deepseek v3.2/v4 DSML parsing code, found by code reading on main @ 110965c. the third one is demonstrated with a runnable repro below.

| # | site | issue |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `lmdeploy/deepseek_v4_encoding.py:694-750`, same pattern in `deepseek_v32_encoding.py:348-385` | `parse_message_from_completion_text` documents "will raise ValueError for malformed output" but enforces the format with `assert`. in practice it raises `AssertionError`, and under `python -O` the checks vanish entirely and malformed output parses into a well-formed-looking message |
| 2 | `deepseek_v4_encoding.py:653/:685` (batch, requires literal `'>\n'` separators) vs `serve/parsers/tool_parser/deepseek_v32_tool_parser.py:91/:131/:223` (streaming, whitespace-tolerant) | the batch reference parser and the serving streaming parser implement different grammars. output with e.g. `'> '` between tags fails the batch parser but streams fine, so the two paths disagree on what "valid DSML" means |
| 3 | `deepseek_v4_encoding.py:679-680` (batch: duplicate parameter name raises `ValueError`) vs `deepseek_v32_tool_parser.py:157-174` (streaming: emits both, producing arguments JSON with duplicate keys) | duplicate parameters are rejected in one path and silently accepted with ambiguous JSON in the other |

i found no production caller for `parse_message_from_completion_text` yet (tests only), so the practical impact today is limited to the module acting as the reference definition of the format; the streaming parser is the production surface and it is the lenient side of divergences 2 and 3.

### Reproduction

for issue 1, loading the module standalone (it only imports stdlib) and calling it with a malformed completion (no eos, no tool-call block, e.g. output cut off by an early stop string):

```python
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('dsv4', 'lmdeploy/deepseek_v4_encoding.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)
m.parse_message_from_completion_text('partial answer, no terminal to', 'chat')
```

observed on python 3.10.11, main @ 110965c:

```
actual: AssertionError: Invalid format: missing EOS token
```

the same call under `python -O` returns normally:

```
{'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'partial answer, no terminal to', 'reasoning_content': '', 'tool_calls': []}
```

so the documented ValueError never occurs, and with asserts stripped the function cannot detect the malformed output at all. happy to extend this to a unit test if the maintainers want the exceptions converted to ValueError raises.

### Environment

- python 3.10.11, lmdeploy main @ 110965c (module loaded standalone, no torch needed for the repro)
- no server run involved, pure parsing call

### Error traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro.py", line 6, in <module>
    m.parse_message_from_completion_text('partial answer, no terminal to', 'chat')
  File "lmdeploy/deepseek_v4_encoding.py", line 731, in parse_message_from_completion_text
    assert stop_token == eos_token, 'Invalid format: missing EOS token'
AssertionError: Invalid format: missing EOS token
```

items.title: [Bug] PyTorch engine: Qwen3.5 hybrid-GDN + AWQ checkpoint crashes on TP>1 - 'AwqLinear' object has no attribute 'block_size'
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.

### Describe the bug

**Environment**: lmdeploy 0.16.0 (latest), Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 12.8 runtime.
**Hardware**: 2 x RTX 2080 Ti 22GB (Turing SM75), NVLink, TP=2.
**Model**: community true-AWQ export of Qwen3.8-27B (`quantization_config: {"quant_method": "awq", "bits": 4, "group_size": 128}`, separate MTP tensors). Qwen3.8-27B is a hybrid model: 48x `linear_attention` + 16x `full_attention` layers.

**What happens**: with `--backend pytorch --tp 2`, the engine subprocess dies during weight loading (`RPCServerDeadError`). Root cause frames below.

**Root cause analysis**

`Qwen3_5TextModel._patch_qkv_weight_loader()` overrides `mod.weight_loader` for the fused GDN QKV projection (non-uniform sections `[key_dim, key_dim, value_dim]`). When a loaded 2D tensor has `shape[0] < sum(sections)` it assumes a fp8-style **scale** shrunk along dim0 and computes `bs = mod.block_size`. For AWQ checkpoints the module is `AwqLinear`, which carries **`group_size`** instead of `block_size` -> AttributeError.

Two extra hazards worth addressing together:

1. `AwqLinear.setup_loaders()` routes ALL four params (`qweight`, `scales`, `qzeros`, `bias`) through `mod.weight_loader`. AWQ `qweight` is transposed-packed (`dim0 ~= in_features/pack`), so the shape heuristic `shape[0] < sum(sections)` can misclassify a `qweight` as a scale and mis-split it -> silent corruption instead of a crash.
2. Suggested fix: branch explicitly on `param._weight_type` (`'qweight' | 'scales' | 'qzeros' | 'bias'`, already set by `setup_loaders()`), shrink scales/qzeros by `group_size`, and handle the transposed `qweight` separately.

TP=1 does not trigger the bug (`mod.is_tp == False` -> `default_weight_loader`). TurboMind backend loads the same artifacts fine; this affects the PyTorch engine path only. Happy to test any fix - failing artifact and hardware are on hand.

### Reproduction

lmdeploy serve api_server /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-MTP --backend pytorch --tp 2 --server-port 8002             Crashes while loading safetensors shards; the engine child process exits before the server comes up.

### Environment

```Shell
- lmdeploy 0.16.0 (pip, latest), torch 2.x cu12x
- Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04
- 2x RTX 2080 Ti 22GB modded (SM75), NVLink
- Model: shawnw3i/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-MTP (autoawq format, group_size 128)
```

### Error traceback

```Shell
File ".../lmdeploy/pytorch/models/qwen3_5.py", line 1249, in load_weights
    load_weight(param, loaded_weight)
File ".../lmdeploy/pytorch/weight_loader/model_weight_loader.py", line 22, in load_weight
    param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, **kwargs)
File ".../lmdeploy/pytorch/models/qwen3_5.py", line 503, in qkv_weight_loader
    bs = mod.block_size
AttributeError: 'AwqLinear' object has no attribute 'block_size'

(via ray::RayWorkerWrapper.build_model() -> RPCServerDeadError: PyTorch ZMQ engine process is not alive.)
```
